newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia rubber extends fall at close.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia rubber extends fall at close.

text.p: Malaysian rubber prices extended losses at the close due to weak consumer demand, traders said.
They said that with no sign of buyers returning to the market, prices were likely to remain soft in the short term.
"Everybody is waiting for the market to drop further hoping that buyers will return," said one local trader. He expects another two to three cents drop next week.
Traders said that though the recent wintering has tightened supply of raw materials, stocks were building up due to weak demand.
At the close, May RSS1 buyer was quoted by the Malaysian Rubber Exchange and Licensing Board at 290.50 cents ($1.16) a kg, unchanged from Thursday.
May SMR 20 buyer was down one cent to 275 cents ($1.10).
Trading houses quoted SMR CV at 346 cents a kg, SMR L at 325, SMR 10 at 278 and drum latex at 233-235 FOB.
The INRO five-day moving average was 222.86 Malaysian/Singapore cents per kg on April 10 against 223.61 on April 9. The daily indicator price was 221.64 versus 222.38.
